newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. says first Rwanda aid plane set to depart.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says first Rwanda aid plane set to depart.

text.p: The U.S. air force said on Tuesday it was loading the first of its cargo planes set to help in the Rwandan refugee crisis. The aircraft was scheduled to leave Germany for Kigali at 1900 GMT.
"We expect to send part of a tanker airlift control unit to set up the preliminary controls for the region," a spokesman at Rhein-Main air base told Reuters.

The spokesman said the C-17 aircraft was being loaded with equipment to allow U.S. forces to set up an air traffic control system at Kigali airport. Also being loaded was equipment needed to off-load humanitarian supplies on subsequent flights.
"There are no armed troops on the flight to clear the way," he said.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said earlier on Tuesday that the United States had changed its plans to send security troops to Zaire and instead would provide fewer than 1,000 military logistics personnel to aid refugees in Rwanda.

Perry said that the situation in central Africa remained fluid and, while a Canadian-led multinational force would now operate chiefly in Rwanda, Washington was ready to send protective troops to Zaire if necessary.
